boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Hendrix College spaces where students study, make art, attend programs, exercise, gather, and spend time outdoors.

cards.title: Use Bailey Library for the full study setup
cards.subtitle: Collections, computers, writing support, and 24-hour study rooms
cards.notes: Bring research and writing work here when you need collections, a computer lab, writing help, or a study room beyond regular library hours.
cards.short_summary: A single academic stop combining research collections with several kinds of student workspaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix states that Bailey Library contains its print and electronic collections, a student computer lab, writing lab, media facilities, and 24-hour study rooms.
cards.access_notes: The cited page documents 24-hour study rooms but does not state building-wide hours or public access; confirm current access locally.

cards.title: Build the group presentation at Oathout
cards.subtitle: Collaborative technology inside the SLTC
cards.notes: Use the technology-equipped work areas for a shared assignment or multimedia presentation, especially when a group needs more than laptops alone.
cards.short_summary: An SLTC workspace designed around collaborative coursework and multimedia preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix says students can work collaboratively on assignments using technology throughout the Oathout Educational Technology Center and prepare multimedia research presentations.
cards.source_title: What's Inside the SLTC | Hendrix College
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Student Life and Technology Center; the cited page does not provide current room hours or entry rules.

cards.title: Check Worsham when campus programming moves indoors
cards.subtitle: The SLTC’s concert, lecture, dance, and performance room
cards.notes: Look for scheduled concerts, lectures, performances, and student programs here; verify the event listing because the room is programmed, not open-use space.
cards.short_summary: A flexible student-programming venue on the first floor of the SLTC.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix identifies Worsham as a 6,000-square-foot space used for concerts, dances, lectures, cultural programs, and performances serving the campus community.
cards.source_title: What's Inside the SLTC | Hendrix College
cards.access_notes: Attend through a scheduled campus program or event; the source does not document unrestricted drop-in access.

cards.title: Use Windgate as a change-of-pace learning stop
cards.subtitle: Exhibitions and student-centered programs in the Miller Creative Quad
cards.notes: Walk through the current exhibition or pair a visit with a museum program; check closures first because the museum follows the College calendar.
cards.short_summary: A campus teaching museum where exhibitions extend learning beyond classrooms and studios.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum presents exhibitions, educational programs, and social activities for Hendrix students and the community and publishes current visiting hours and school-calendar closures.
cards.access_notes: The visit page lists current hours and notes closures for school and national holidays; check it before going.

cards.title: Catch an outdoor performance in the Creative Quad
cards.subtitle: A central courtyard framed by Hendrix arts spaces
cards.notes: Watch departmental calendars for courtyard concerts and arts events, then use the named rain location when weather changes the plan.
cards.short_summary: The open center of the Creative Quad doubles as a documented outdoor performance site.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hendrix Wind Ensemble lists a Concert in the Quad at the Miller Creative Quad Courtyard, with Staples Auditorium as the rain location.
cards.source_title: Hendrix College Wind Ensemble | Hendrix College
cards.access_notes: Use for scheduled outdoor events or ordinary campus circulation; event access and weather plans vary by program.

cards.title: Try the wall with Hendrix’s climbing community
cards.subtitle: Climbing practice inside the Wellness and Athletics Center
cards.notes: Connect with the Climbing Coalition before using the wall so you can learn the applicable schedule, equipment process, and facility rules.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated indoor practice feature used by Hendrix’s student climbing organization.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix documents a climbing wall in the Wellness and Athletics Center and says the student Climbing Coalition uses it for practice.
cards.access_notes: WAC access rules, supervision, and wall availability may apply; confirm with the facility or Climbing Coalition before participating.

cards.title: Choose the pool for a lower-impact workout
cards.subtitle: An eight-lane pool adjoining the WAC
cards.notes: Check the current pool schedule before arriving, then bring any required Hendrix identification and follow posted aquatic-center policies.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated swimming facility with recreational use documented for WAC members and guests.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix describes the Aquatic Center as an eight-lane pool with a diving area, sun porch, and retractable roof that WAC members and guests can use.
cards.access_notes: Pool schedules, WAC membership or guest rules, and aquatic policies apply; consult the current WAC page before visiting.

cards.title: Learn why campus events keep returning to the Brick Pit
cards.subtitle: A central outdoor performance and gathering space
cards.notes: Use the stepped space for an announced program or group meetup, and leave room for scheduled events that rely on it as a performance site.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable central venue used for orientation gatherings and major student performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix calls the Brick Pit a central campus performance spot, and the 2025 orientation schedule used it for the class photo and orientation-group dinner.
cards.source_title: Hendrix College Class of ’29 Orientation Move-in Day Schedule
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; scheduled programs may control use, and the cited orientation activities were date-specific.

cards.title: Meet outdoors where student groups already gather
cards.subtitle: A landscaped court beside Butler Plaza
cards.notes: Suggest Pecan Court for a daytime club meetup or casual outdoor break, then check the campus calendar for programs already using the space.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor court with documented club meetings and orientation activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix’s club directory identifies Pecan Court as a weekly meeting place for a student organization, while the 2025 orientation schedule placed Warrior Welcome activities there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space shared with organized activities; check current event reservations and weather conditions.

cards.title: Pause among native plants at Stellar Joy Garden
cards.subtitle: A pollinator garden within the Art Complex
cards.notes: Follow the garden paths, read the educational signs, and use the student-made seating without disturbing plants, pollinators, or the koi pond.
cards.short_summary: A student-built garden designed for ecological learning, rest, and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix reports that students helped create the Stellar Joy Garden for the campus community to learn, rest, and reflect, adding native plants, paths, educational signs, and seating.
cards.source_title: Hendrix Professor, Students Create New Native Plant Garden | Hendrix College
cards.access_notes: Located within the Art Complex; the source does not specify hours, gate status, accessibility details, or unrestricted public access.
